reviews.text:
Terrible service, my dog ​​was there for a week. When I picked her up, she was dirty and smelled bad.
She was very thirsty, very short of breath, and very scared. She's running away from something we still don't understand what it is, and she wants to sleep next to us, something that has never happened before.
I'm afraid she was mistreated because she's not the same dog that came home.
The staff are extremely unfriendly and show no affection for the animals.
I wouldn't recommend them to anyone.

Please do not ignore all recent 1-star reviews associated with Dogga. If you are looking for a place that guarantees the true well-being of your pet and transparent and respectful treatment of clients, I recommend you read this review.

We left our dog at the hotel for several days and she returned with clear signs of neglect and lack of well-being: she showed a serious behavioral regression (she started relieving herself inside the house again) and revealed an extreme and atypical hunger in the following days, something that had never happened before. The state in which she was returned to us left us with the clear conviction that she did not receive the proper care during her stay.

In addition to the poor quality of service provided to the animal, the management demonstrated total incivility and verbal disrespect towards me, my wife, and my children aged 8 and 5. I decided to immediately pay for the alleged material damages presented by the management on site, hoping to end any connection with the school.

However, 15 days after the service ended, we were surprised with an invoice for €363 relating to a "30-day notice period" and charges for "theoretical classes" that were never taught. When we requested proof of a signed contract justifying these charges, they immediately resorted to emails from a lawyer demanding payment, without ever presenting any signed document or digital proof of acceptance of their terms and conditions. This practice of intimidating lawyers is unfortunately common, as can be seen in other reviews.

I also challenge readers of this review to carefully read the management's responses to all recent negative reviews. It reveals a pattern of arrogance, blame-shifting, and a lack of accountability that is very telling. The same will surely happen in response to this review.

Disappointing experience – aggressive sales and unprofessional training

I chose this school for its location and enrolled my 6-month-old puppy for basic training. While the initial talk sounded reasonable, the experience quickly became uncomfortable.

There was strong pressure to buy expensive extras, including equipment and €200 theoretical videos in Portuguese, even after clearly refusing them. This aggressive upselling felt disrespectful.

The training itself was very basic and focused more on promoting the trainer’s “unique method” than on helping the dog. When our puppy showed stress, it was ignored, and questions were answered sarcastically rather than constructively.

In the final session, without warning, multiple off-leash dogs were released around our puppy as an “evaluation,” creating a highly stressful and unrealistic situation. We were then blamed for our puppy’s normal reactions, and the session was filmed.

At the end, Pedro refused to continue working with our dog, saying he felt a “lack of trust,” leaving us without guidance or support.

Overall, the main issues were aggressive sales tactics, lack of empathy, poor communication, and stressful training methods. I would not recommend this place, especially for young puppies or owners expecting respectful guidance.

Dear Mr. Mikjail Salazar,

We were unable to identify any service contracted or attended in your name at Dogga Academy in our records, including the "Dog Training" service mentioned in this review.

Therefore, we cannot link the one-star rating and the comment "Very expensive" to any service experience we may have had with you.

Dogga's prices are communicated and known before contracting, and it is naturally legitimate for each person to make their own assessment regarding the price.

If you have indeed contracted or attended any service at Dogga Academy, please indicate in whose name the contract was made so that we can identify the situation and respond concretely.

My dog ​​Spike and I are loving the reactivity management classes.
Walks with Spike have become much calmer, both for him and for me, as his tutor.
The progress has been significant. In each session we manage to evolve and improve.
We learned that we should have had classes when he was little. Not when we already have a problem to solve.
We are very grateful for the support at Dogga and we recommend them.

If someone had told me a few months ago that today I would be able to take the first steps walking King with more peace of mind and confidence, I would hardly have believed it.

King is a Serra da Estrela dog who entered the peak of adolescence at a time when our lives changed completely. We moved house, routines, and space. What seemed like just an adaptation to me was a real emotional shake-up for him. Little by little, he began to show signs of insecurity, anxiety, and reactivity. Everything that was new or unpredictable became a potential threat in his eyes. Unfortunately, this escalation culminated in a biting incident, which left me deeply shaken and clueless about what I was going to do about King and whether I would ever be able to fully trust the situation again. And he, in me. It was at that moment that I found Dogga.

Initially, I was looking for someone to "correct" King's behavior. Today I realize that this was only a small part of what we really needed.

Dogga taught me something that completely changed how I looked at King: before a behavior exists, there is always an emotion, and simply shifting the focus from being "owners" to being "guardians" helps with the understanding and patience needed to communicate with the dog. Throughout the program, I also realized a difficult reality to accept: often, we, the guardians, unintentionally contribute to these behaviors. Out of ignorance, we reinforce wrong attitudes, communicate unclearly, and allow our own anxiety, fear, and frustration to be passed on to the dog. They experience our emotional state much more than we imagine. They sense when we are tense, insecure, or worried and end up taking on a protective role because they believe we can't handle the situation.

King wasn't a "bad," "dominant," or "aggressive" dog. He was an insecure, anxious dog trying to survive in the only way he knew how. Like any animal, he made decisions based on what he had learned on his own to ensure his own safety. The biggest transformation didn't just happen to King. It happened to me. I'm learning to communicate better with him, to interpret his body language, to recognize the signs of stress before they turn into explosions, and above all, to be the safe haven he needed. I'm learning to stop reacting impulsively and start acting with knowledge, calm, and consistency. The results are absolutely incredible. King is becoming a much more balanced, more confident, and much less reactive dog, with increasingly shorter self-regulation times. There are still challenges, because changing deep emotions takes time, but today I know better how to help him and how to continue building on this evolution. Every small achievement has enormous significance for both of us.

The Dogga program goes far beyond dog training. It's a true education program for owners. It teaches us to understand that dogs are not human and that they don't interpret the world as we do. They communicate differently, learn differently, and react according to what they feel, not what we would like them to feel.

To the entire Dogga team, my sincerest thanks 🫂 Thank you for never making me feel judged (neither me nor King), for restoring hope when it was completely lost, and above all, for teaching us that changing a dog always begins with changing how we communicate with them and our attitude towards the dog and ourselves.

I wholeheartedly recommend Dogga to anyone experiencing difficulties with anxiety, fear, or reactivity in their dog. They don't promise miracles or quick fixes. They teach, accompany, support, and give us the tools to build a true relationship based on trust, respect, and understanding. And that's worth much more than any training. "Little by little, a great love is built."

I loved the experience of having my dog ​​(Zeus) there and I highly recommend them! Dedicated people, with a lot of technical training and always attentive to the animals' needs. A big hug to Pedro and Ana who were truly impeccable!

Dear Pedro Melo,

Thank you so much for your 5 stars!

Even without words, your review means a lot to us. Knowing that your experience was positive enough to deserve the highest rating is a huge source of pride for the entire team.

At Dogga, we believe that every dog, every owner, and every visit should end exactly as the best stories begin: with the desire to return.

We hope to continue earning your trust for many years to come and, who knows, maybe on your next visit you'll tell us a little more about your experience. We always love to hear the stories behind the stars.

Thank you so much for being part of the Dogga family.

Best regards,

The Dogga Team 🐾

I would like to express my gratitude to Dogga for the exceptional care and affection with which they treat my dog. He always comes and goes happy, which for us is the greatest sign of trust and well-being. It is also very gratifying to see that he likes all the members of the team, reflecting the welcoming atmosphere and dedication that one feels there. Thank you very much for all the care and professionalism.

After several months at this school, I realized that animal welfare is secondary. The priority is undoubtedly selling products and services.
Mr. Pedro and the blonde lady at reception are extremely arrogant. They don't accept criticism or opposing opinions. And proof of this is the response they gave to my negative review.
They say they don't have any records of me. Were they deleted during the blackout that hit the Iberian Peninsula?
Because I remember paying for an evaluation consultation; more than €200 for some classes that looked like Tupperware meetings, where the objective is simply to sell dog supplies; and the monthly fees paid.
This negative review doesn't seem strange at all to me. Just do a little research to realize that it's not the first, nor the second. And I can say with certainty that it won't be the last. It's also possible to see a certain consistency in the reasons for these reviews.
In conclusion, I don't recommend it to anyone.
I'm very happy with Petra's rapid progress. I know I'll get the Petra I want. Thank you. 👍 …

I recommend Dogga, they have an excellent service in all aspects.
I sought out Dogga because I was pregnant and worried because Teddy didn't like being in the same space as children, even if they were family. To avoid conflicts, we never had any kind of family gatherings at my house. I learned about Dogga through Porto Canal, I saw several interviews and the one that caught my attention was the interview where they presented their newly released book "My dog ​​is going to have a human sibling". I booked an evaluation appointment without thinking twice. I must say that the consultation was super pleasant, Pedro Runa is an excellent and fun professional. During the consultation, Pedro prepared a work plan that would prepare Teddy for the arrival of the baby. I learned many things that I didn't even know were possible. When André was born, Pedro once again helped put into practice what we learned throughout the sessions, André's smells, the breastfeeding position, among other things. The help of Pedro and the team was very important to me, we have had unique experiences, we already have family gatherings at home, always respecting Teddy's space. Our problem is solved, our Teddy has never growled at any other child in the family again, and with André it has been an incredible experience.

Thank you Dogga
Thank you Pedro Runa

I leave my dog ​​Tobias at the Dogga Residence Drop & Go every week, and the experience has been truly transformative.

Tobias is a small dog who has always been very spoiled and ended up developing separation anxiety. For a long time, it was practically impossible to leave him alone at home, even for just a few hours.

With the help of the Dogga team and the Drop & Go routine, he has gradually become accustomed to being in other environments calmly and safely. What impressed me most was the attention they give to each dog's behavior and the calm way they handle the adaptation.

Today I can leave Tobias alone at home for a few hours, something that seemed impossible before.

For anyone who has a dog that suffers when left alone, this service really makes a difference. It's a huge relief to know that he's in a safe place, well cared for, and with people who truly understand dog behavior.

Dogga changes lives and connects families, that's their motto and it's the purest truth.
Our Pandora is a rescued dog who went through several families before arriving with us. When she arrived at our home, she had marks of mistreatment, and the marks weren't just physical; whenever we approached Pandora, she showed fearful behaviors, that is, she trembled, whined, and urinated. We sought out Dogga to try to help our Pandora, and Pedro and his team were very attentive to our Pandora.
Without a doubt, the programs that Pandora did helped her a lot. Today, we are part of Dogga as guardians, and our Pandora is a student. Whenever we arrive at Dogga to drop her off, she gets super happy. When she sees the trainers, she goes to greet them. Pandora loves Dogga, which made us super comfortable when we left her at the hotel. It was a very positive experience at the hotel; in addition to the excellent conditions, the affection with which Pandora was treated was very satisfying for both us and our princess. Pandora is a happy dog, that was always our goal when we rescued her. Dogga made it possible and not only changed Pandora's life but also ours. We love the hotel and will continue to use their services because we are very satisfied. Thank you Dogga.

I have two Scottish Terriers, Balu and Sun, who have always been quite anxious when away from us. For a long time, we thought it simply wouldn't be possible to leave them in a kennel, and therefore our holidays were always very limited.

The Dogga team suggested starting with the Drop & Go service, precisely to help the dogs gradually get used to the environment and routines. It was a process done very calmly, respecting their behavior and paying enormous attention to every detail.

Thanks to this preparation, we were finally able to do something that hadn't happened in a long time: spend 8 days of Carnival holiday with the peace of mind of knowing that Balu and Sun were okay.

During their stay at Dogga Residence, the dogs were very well cared for, and it's clear that there is a real concern for the well-being and behavioral aspects of each dog.

If this preparation phase with Drop & Go hadn't existed, we probably would never have reached this point. It was a very positive experience, both for us and for our dogs.

We have so much to thank Dogga for, for everything they've done for our family, especially for our Dimitry.
When we were about to give up, Dogga was the only one who showed us the light at the end of the tunnel. Our Dimitry came to us when he was two months old, and as time went on, Dimitry began to have negative reactions towards our 6-year-old daughter, trying to bite her several times. Dimitry's behavior worsened to the point that we couldn't take walks in the street in peace. Every outing was too stressful because our dog wanted to attack everything he saw: children, people, and any animal he saw. We tried to find help, but everywhere we went it only got worse, and we didn't like the type of training they did, as we considered it too violent. That's when we met Dogga, and, already without hope, we scheduled an evaluation appointment. I went into the consultation without any hope, but I left with the utmost faith that everything would work out, and we weren't wrong. We realized that the problem was never Dimitry, but rather us as guardians. We came to this conclusion ourselves from the moment Pedro showed us what was happening that was causing Dimitry to have those behaviors. With the help of the team and Pedro Runa, we started working as a team for Dimitry's well-being. Today, Dimitry is a sociable dog and loves children. Dogga is our second family.
With the recent opening of the hotel, we didn't think twice about leaving our furry friends there. Yes, today Dimitry's social group is larger 😍. The hotel has excellent facilities, and the treatment remains the same: excellent.
Dogga changed our family's life.
Thank you for everything you have done for us.

I want to express my gratitude to Dogga.
My dog ​​has always been quite fearful and had difficulty interacting with other dogs and new environments. Since she started attending the academy, I've noticed an incredible improvement in her behavior.
The team has always shown great patience, affection, and professionalism, creating a safe environment where she gradually gained confidence. Today I see her much calmer, more sociable, and happier.
It's truly reassuring to know that she's in a place where she's well cared for and understood.
I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a trustworthy place for their dogs.

Unfortunately, I had a very negative experience with Dogga after an incident with my dog, Venus. I do not recommend this place.

One day while she was at the academy, Venus returned home with a mouth injury consistent with a bite, a situation that was not communicated to me at the time of collection. I only realized it when I got home.

Later, the owner of the company explained that the injury could have occurred during a training session with a flirt pole, when she tried to catch the ball with intensity. Accidents can happen in a training context, that's understandable.

What surprised me was how the situation was handled. At no point did Dogga show any interest in knowing about Venus's health or in monitoring the evolution of the injury.

Instead, I received an email from a company lawyer, with an intimidating tone, denying that there was any proof that the injury had occurred within Dogga and focusing only on collecting the monthly fee due to the notice period clause—even though I never objected to fulfilling that obligation.

What disappointed me most was not the incident itself, but the lack of care, communication, and concern for the animal's well-being.

When we leave our dogs in the care of others, we expect professionalism, transparency, and responsibility. Unfortunately, in this case, that trust was compromised.
